summary:
A procedure is a custom command created by the programmer.

A procedure is a type of sprite which can animate automatically.

A procedure is a command which affects the backdrop only.

A procedure is a sound effect for animal sprites.
Procedures help organize long scripts.
Procedures make scripts longer and messier.
Procedures remove all sprites.
Procedures change the Scratch editor.
The My Blocks category is used to create procedures.
The Motion category is used to create procedures.
The Looks category is used to create procedures.
The Sound category is used to create procedures.
Procedures can be reused multiple times in a project.
Procedures can only be used once.
Procedures only work with sounds.
Procedures only work with backdrops.
Using procedures can make code easier to read.
Using procedures makes code harder to understand for new users.
Using procedures hides all code.
Using procedures removes comments.
A custom block can contain several instructions grouped together.
A custom block can only contain one instruction.
A custom block cannot contain code.
A custom block only contains sounds.
Debugging means finding and fixing problems in a project.
Debugging means creating new sprites.
Debugging means drawing costumes.
Debugging means changing the stage size.
After creating a custom block, it can be used like a new command.
After creating a custom block, the project ends.
After creating a custom block, all sprites disappear.
After creating a custom block, the backdrop is deleted.
